summary.intent: Close the race in which two addrConn.connect() calls both saw Idle and both started tryAllAddrs, orphaning a transport (issue 7365), by holding ac.mu from the idle check through the Connecting transition.
summary.issue_fit: Met: connect() and updateAddrs() now hand ac.mu to resetTransportAndUnlock(), so the second connect sees Connecting; the 100000-run flake measurement is a supporting assertion not reproduced here.
summary.coverage: Full diff of clientconn.go, both callers, onClose, tearDown and the health-check state route reviewed; two focused tests passed at the head; two lock-handoff premises verified as holding.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -race -count=1 -run 'Test$/(DialWithBlockErrorOnBadCertificates|ResetConnectBackoff|UpdateAddresses|TestConnectivity|CanceledCtx)' .` at the reviewed head: ok in 1.1s; subtests matched were not listed (no -v).

Reviewer ran `go test -race -count=1 -v -run 'Test/AuthorityRevive' ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests` at the reviewed head: PASS (0.13s); one pass does not reproduce the 0.4% flake, so it is not evidence the race is closed.

Environment note: after the runs, empty read-only placeholder files (`.claude/*`, `.mcp.json`) were listed as untracked in the clone; the sandbox appears to have created them, the tracked tree and HEAD are unchanged, and they were left in place.

observations.fact: The change adds no regression test; the race is probabilistic and the only stated evidence is the existing Test/AuthorityRevive flake rate.
observations.evidence: `clientconn.go` is the only changed file (git diff --stat main...review-head).

observations.fact: The health-check callback is a second route into Connecting, but it only acts while ac.transport == currentTr, so it cannot start from Idle.

requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:905-923 and 1234-1262: no unlock between the Idle check and updateConnectivityState(Connecting); a second connect() blocks on ac.mu and sees Connecting.

requirements.evidence: A 100000-attempt measurement was not repeated; one reviewer run of Test/AuthorityRevive passed, which cannot show a 0.4% flake is gone. Nothing material depends on it because the fix is established by the lock-handoff trace.

tasks.premise: At the head, the only transition of an addrConn into Connecting is the updateConnectivityState(Connecting) inside resetTransportAndUnlock, and connect() reaches it with ac.mu held continuously from its Idle check, so two concurrent connect() calls cannot both start tryAllAddrs for the same ctx.

At the head, both callers enter resetTransportAndUnlock holding ac.mu once, every path unlocks exactly once, and nothing run under the lock or after the handoff in updateAddrs can wait on a lock the same goroutine holds, so no double unlock, leak or deadlock is introduced.
